title: Tested like us (Hebrews 2:14–18)
hookLine: he was made like us in every way, so he can help the tested
tomorrow: a throne you're invited to walk right up to?

cards: Press two fingers to the inside of your wrist and part of today's answer is right there, ticking. Flesh and blood.

Hebrews spends its first chapter setting the Son very high, above the angels, at the right hand of the Majesty. Then chapter two comes straight back down to the ground: a body, the fear of death, temptation.
Was he ever really tempted, in a body like ours? The writer says yes, and says why that matters.

teach.b: "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same." The children are flesh and blood, so he took flesh and blood.

teach.h: FREED FROM THE FEAR OF DEATH.
teach.b: Through death, the writer says, he set free those "who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage." A whole life held by a fear: the writer names it plainly, and says its grip can be broken.

teach.h: MADE LIKE HIS BRETHREN IN ALL THINGS.
teach.b: Then the key line: "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest." In all things. Not a visitor in a costume.
And watch that title, high priest: the coming chapters keep returning to it.
And the last verse gives the reason: "For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted."

Succour is the old word for help, for running to someone's aid. Christians read this as a reason to bring a struggle to him at all: the help doesn't come from a distance. It comes from someone who has felt the pull.
The Gospels tell it too: in the wilderness, after fasting, hungry, and tested. So yes. Tested like us, in the same skin.

how: Some Christians bring a temptation or a hard trial to Jesus in prayer by name, trusting, as Hebrews 2:18 says, that he is able to help.

o: made like us in all things, and so able to help
kept far from all trouble by the angels
given easy tests so nobody would fail

games.q: flesh and blood — tap the pairs.
p: what he shared with the children
what he set people free from

s: Hebrews says the Son only seemed to have a body
"he also himself likewise took part of the same": flesh and blood.
Hebrews says he was tempted, and so can help the tempted
"he is able to succour them that are tempted."
succour is the old word for help, for running to someone's aid.

games.q: a friend is too ashamed to pray about the habit she keeps falling back into. 'he'd never get it,' she says. what does Hebrews 2 say?
o: he was made like his brethren in all things, tempted, and so able to help.
he was above temptation, so she should fix it first, then pray.
only big temptations count; small habits aren't worth bringing.
games.why: in all things it behoved him to be made like his brethren, and because he was tempted, he is able to succour the tempted.

practice: Find your pulse, at the wrist or the side of your neck, and rest two fingers there. Feel it keep time for a few breaths: flesh and blood, the very thing Hebrews says he shared.

Then let one pull you know well come to mind, a habit, a temper, a worry, and hold it beside that steady beat without fighting it. Nothing needs solving in these two minutes; the pulse and the pull can simply sit side by side.

wordCard.voice: Tested like us. Hebrews two: the Son made like his brethren in all things, tempted, and so able to help the tempted, from the inside.

orig.note: Greek: to test or to tempt; the verb behind tempted in Hebrews 2:18.
